checks.name: Profile ordering
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test sandbox profile_ordering
checks.output: 3 tests pass. compare() returns a four-valued ProfileOrdering, never a bool: observe vs observe = Identical, observe vs workspace-offline = Narrower, the reverse = Wider, workspace-offline vs workspace-egress = Narrower. Incomparable is reachable and symmetric: WritableWithGrants+Denied against ReadOnlySnapshot+BrokeredAny returns Incomparable in both directions. The order is now also the combining rule for whole specs: ProfileOrdering::combine is exercised directly and Narrower.combine(Wider) = Incomparable, Wider.combine(Narrower) = Incomparable, Identical.combine(Narrower) = Narrower, Incomparable.combine(Identical) = Incomparable, so a disagreeing axis cannot resolve to the permissive one. evaluate_reuse still preserves Incomparable by routing it to RequiresNewHost.

checks.name: Spec immutability and completeness
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test sandbox spec_completeness; cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --doc sandbox::SandboxSpec; then rustc compile probes for the private-field assignment and the omitted field
checks.output: 7 integration tests plus 4 doctests pass. Immutability: `compiled.actor = Actor::new("globex", "mallory").unwrap()` fails standalone under rustc --edition 2024 with E0616 "field `actor` of struct `SandboxSpec` is private", and the paired read `compiled.actor()` compiles; the type exposes no setter. Completeness: SandboxSpec now carries 16 private fields covering every clause of the requirement's field list, and every one is required by construction — omitting `actor` from the SandboxSpecParts literal fails standalone with E0063 "missing field `actor` in initializer of `SandboxSpecParts`", while the complete literal differing by exactly that line compiles (both run as doctests). The coverage table the row asks for is SPEC_FIELD_COVERAGE in tests/sandbox.rs: 20 named requirement clauses, each with a probe that reads the value back off a compiled spec (profile ID, profile version, policy digest, tenant, actor, provider account, workspace security-context hash, immutable base revision, readable path grants, writable path grants, the five allowlists, provider-control policy, tool-workload policy, credential descriptors with their exact process class, the eight budgets, required features, accepted enforcement implementation digests, nested isolation, approval revision, prohibited capabilities); the table is asserted to name each clause once and to have exactly 20 rows. The ten accessors the previous audit found missing now exist and were exercised: actor, provider_account, workspace_context, base_revision, path_grants, tool_allowlist, credential_descriptors, nested_isolation, approval_revision, enforcement_implementation_digests. Dangerous states were removed rather than rejected: tenant is read off identity::Actor (which has no constructor without a tenant) so spec tenant and actor cannot disagree; provider_account reuses the crate's existing models::ProviderAccountId rather than minting a second one; digests are TaggedDigest<Domain> so `let workspace: WorkspaceContextHash = policy` fails with E0308 (verified standalone) while the same binding into PolicyDigest compiles; paths are SandboxPath (absolute, no empty or . / .. component); budgets are eight named categories rather than a list, so a spec missing the spool or artifact budget does not compile. Component validation, which used to live in compile(), now lives in the component constructors and is measured: 13 assertions covering digest length ("sha256:policy" -> digest_length), missing algorithm, unknown algorithm, uppercase hex, relative path, traversal path, empty component, empty allowlist name, empty required-feature set, empty accepted-implementation set, zero process group, zero Landlock ABI and zero namespace inode. Duplicate path grants and duplicate credential descriptors are refused with category duplicate_entry rather than silently merged. compile() itself now refuses a spec wider than its profile with category widens_profile on tool_workload_egress and on path_grants. The previous test `a_spec_cannot_be_compiled_with_an_empty_required_field` was replaced by `a_component_cannot_be_built_from_an_invalid_value`, which asserts strictly more. Negative controls: breaking the tool allowlist accessor, the duplicate-grant refusal, the digest length check and the widens-profile refusal each made the matching test fail, and each was restored.

checks.name: No silent downgrade
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test sandbox no_silent_downgrade
checks.output: 3 tests pass. A spec requiring [cgroup_v2, landlock_abi_3] admitted on a host offering only cgroup_v2 fails with SandboxError::RequiredEnforcementMissing{feature:"landlock_abi_3"} — the feature is named. Negotiation is exhausted over the two-feature power set: all three incomplete host sets ([], [cgroup_v2], [landlock_abi_3]) refuse with category required_enforcement_missing and the complete set admits. admit_on returns Result<(), SandboxError>, so its success type carries no profile and there is no value in which a weaker resolution could be returned. New in this pass: the accepted enforcement-implementation digests are compared rather than merely stored — a host offering landlock_abi_3 through implementation sha256:00..63 when the spec accepts only sha256:00..0c refuses with category enforcement_implementation_rejected naming both the feature and the rejected digest. Negative control: deleting the `required.accepts(offer.implementation())` check made that test fail; restoring it made it pass.

checks.name: Egress split
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test sandbox egress_split; cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --doc; then rustc on the doctest body to capture its error code
checks.output: 2 integration tests pass: a compiled spec carries BrokeredNamed on the control plane and Denied for tool workload simultaneously, and widening the control plane to BrokeredAny leaves the tool-workload policy at Denied. The compile-fail proof executes as 'src/sandbox.rs - sandbox (line 10) - compile fail'; compiling that snippet's body standalone confirms it fails for the intended reason and not incidentally: E0308 "mismatched types: expected ToolWorkloadEgress, found ProviderControlEgress". It is now paired with a passing example that differs only in the type of the value assigned (`let bound: ToolWorkloadEgress = workload`), which executes as an ordinary doctest, so the compile_fail cannot be passing for an unrelated reason. Recorded caveat, unchanged: CI's rust.yml runs `cargo test --workspace --all-targets`, and --all-targets excludes doctests, so this proof is not exercised by CI as configured; it was exercised here by `cargo test --workspace` without --all-targets.

checks.name: Attestation comparison
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test sandbox attestation_comparison; cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --doc sandbox::AdoptedHost sandbox::QuarantinedOperation; then rustc compile probes for AdoptedHost::new and a fourth quarantined operation
checks.output: 7 integration tests plus 4 doctests pass. All five adoption cases are covered and each now names its own reason: matching attestations adopt; a differing seccomp digest quarantines with QuarantineReason::Mismatch{field:"seccomp_digest"}; recorded-but-not-observed gives NoObservedAttestation; observed-but-never-recorded gives NoRecordedAttestation; neither gives NothingAttested. EnforcementAttestation now carries all 12 fields the requirement lists — resolved_paths, namespaces, process_group, cgroup, backend, kernel_boot, supervisor_properties, landlock (ABI plus ruleset digest), seccomp_digest, egress_digest, credential_delivery, external_daemon — each with an accessor, all of which are read in `every_attested_field_is_readable`. The four accessors the previous audit found absent (resolved_paths, process_group, credential_delivery_mode, landlock_abi) exist and return typed values, not strings: ProcessGroupId and LandlockAbi are NonZero-backed, NamespaceIdentity is a kind plus inode, CredentialDelivery is a four-variant enum, and the three digests are domain-tagged. Comparison covers every field and is proven field by field: `every_recorded_field_is_compared` varies each of the 12 alone and asserts the reported field, and the 12 names collected in order equal EnforcementAttestation::COMPARED_FIELDS; varying only the Landlock ruleset digest is also caught, reported as the "landlock" field. first_difference destructures the struct without `..`, so a field added later cannot go uncompared — verified by adding a 13th field and observing rustc error[E0027] (plus E0063 at the constructor). Adoption is still comparison, not reconstruction: AdoptedHost borrows the *recorded* attestation (asserted with std::ptr::eq against the recorded value) and has no public constructor — `AdoptedHost::new(&observed())` fails standalone with E0599 "no function or associated item named `new` found for struct `AdoptedHost<'a>`", paired with a passing example that obtains one only through adopt_host. The permitted-operations clause, which the previous evidence recorded as unmeasurable because it existed only in a doc comment, is now structural: AdoptionOutcome::Quarantined carries a QuarantinedHost whose permitted_operations() returns exactly [Observe, Reconcile, Cancel], and QuarantinedOperation has no other variant — `QuarantinedOperation::ResumeProvider` fails standalone with E0599 "no variant or associated item named `ResumeProvider` found for enum `QuarantinedOperation`", paired with `QuarantinedOperation::Observe`, which compiles and runs. Adopting with nothing recorded is not merely refused but unrepresentable: AdoptedHost borrows an attestation, so there is no value to construct when `recorded` is None. Negative controls: removing the credential_delivery comparison, making a recorded-but-unobserved host adopt, and making the permitted set carry Observe twice each made the matching test fail, and each was restored.

checks.name: Narrowing-only reuse
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test sandbox narrowing_only_reuse
checks.output: 8 tests pass. Identical and narrower requests return ReuseOutcome::Reuse; wider and incomparable requests return RequiresNewHost. Reuse now compares the whole spec rather than the profile alone. Subject identity is checked over 4 cases — a different tenant, a different actor within the tenant, a different provider account and a different workspace security-context hash all return RequiresNewHost; the actor comparison goes through identity::Actor::is_same_as, which refuses to answer across tenants, and treats that refusal as "not provably the same principal". Authority is compared over 9 axes, each widened alone: profile, provider-control egress, tool-workload egress, path grants, allowlists, credential descriptors, budgets, required features and prohibited capabilities all return RequiresNewHost, and each case also asserts the axis really was widened (compare_authority is not Narrower). The mirror table narrows the same 8 axes one at a time and asserts compare_authority == Narrower and ReuseOutcome::Reuse. Nested isolation is ordered: raising nested tools to StrongerIsolation reuses, lowering them to HostBoundary requires a new host. Grants can only narrow: PathGrants exposes narrowed_to (an intersection that also takes the lower access of each shared path) and no union — `existing.union(&requested)` fails standalone with E0599 "no method named `union` found for struct `PathGrants`", paired with a compiling narrowed_to call; the test shows a greedy request cannot add /etc/shadow and cannot raise /opt/toolchain from ReadOnly, and that the intersection in either order stays within the reviewed set. evaluate_reuse still takes two &SandboxSpec and returns an enum, so no path mutates either spec. Negative controls: dropping the provider-account check, dropping the budget axis and dropping the path-grant axis from compare_authority, and taking the higher access in narrowed_to, each made the matching test fail, and each was restored.

checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test sandbox approval_cannot_widen; cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --doc; then rustc on the doctest body to capture its error code

checks.name: Budget typing
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test sandbox budget_typing violation_dispositions::exhaustion_and_violation_are_distinct_classes
checks.output: 4 budget tests plus the distinctness test pass. Budget::new takes a BudgetUnit by value, so a unitless budget has no constructor. BudgetUnit now has 8 variants covering the six budget categories the requirement names; every one accepts exactly its ceiling and rejects ceiling+1 with category budget_out_of_range and a message naming the unit: milliseconds 86400000, memory_bytes 68719476736, cpu_millicores 64000, processes 4096, file_descriptors 65536, temp_bytes 549755813888, spool_bytes 274877906944, artifact_bytes 1099511627776. The four pre-existing units and ceilings are unchanged. The gap the previous audit recorded against this row is closed: a spec now carries a Budgets value with one named field per category (cgroup memory, cgroup CPU, process rlimit, descriptor rlimit, timeout, temporary storage, spool, artifact), each constructed by Budgets::declare with the unit that belongs to it, so a missing category does not compile and a category in the wrong unit is caught — the observed unit sequence is [memory_bytes, cpu_millicores, processes, file_descriptors, milliseconds, temp_bytes, spool_bytes, artifact_bytes]. An over-ceiling spool quantity refuses naming spool_bytes. Exhaustion and violation stay distinct: ViolationClass::BudgetExhaustion != PolicyViolation and their dispositions differ (terminate_run_and_record vs terminate_run). Negative control: declaring the spool budget in temp_bytes made the unit test fail; restoring it made it pass.

checks.name: Violation dispositions
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test sandbox violation_dispositions
checks.output: 4 tests pass, unchanged by this pass. ViolationClass::ALL has exactly the 4 contract classes (policy_violation, budget_exhaustion, enforcement_loss, attestation_mismatch), each has a disposition, all four spellings are distinct, and every disposition is one of TerminateRun, TerminateRunAndRecord or Quarantine. The Disposition enum has exactly three variants and no Continue, so "continue" is unrepresentable rather than merely unused. EnforcementLoss and AttestationMismatch both map to Quarantine.

review.acceptance: No independent reviewer examined this item. The evidence above was written by the implementing agent and every command in it was run in this worktree; it is a self-review and is not independent.

notes: No enforcement was tested and none is claimed. This slice creates no namespace, loads no seccomp filter, applies no Landlock ruleset and allocates no cgroup; every result above is a property of values, comparisons and the type system, measured by running tests, doctests and standalone rustc compile probes. Scope note: the item's contract allows `rust/crates/automonique-protocol/`, and four files in it changed. src/sandbox.rs and tests/sandbox.rs are the item's own. src/models.rs and tests/models.rs changed only because EnforcementAttestation is shared: growing it from 6 fields to the 12 the requirement lists replaced the six-argument `new` with `record(EnforcementAttestationParts)`, so the three doctest preludes in src/models.rs and the one test helper in tests/models.rs that built an attestation were updated mechanically. No models behaviour changed: the helper still returns attestations that differ exactly when its label differs, now by encoding the label into the digest body. Keeping the old constructor was rejected because any six-field constructor would have to invent the other six fields, and an attestation that records "unknown" for credential delivery or process group is the hole this row exists to close. Two design decisions worth a reviewer's attention. First, the spec's tenant is read off identity::Actor rather than stored separately, and the provider account reuses models::ProviderAccountId rather than a second identifier type; both remove a duplicate concept, and the second makes src/sandbox.rs depend on src/models.rs, which already depends on src/sandbox.rs — a mutual module reference that compiles but is a layering smell worth revisiting if either module is split. Second, evaluate_reuse compares policy structurally rather than by digest equality, on the grounds that a new policy digest granting strictly less is exactly the narrowing the requirement permits; a reviewer who disagrees should say so, because it is the one place where "identical or demonstrably narrower" was interpreted rather than transcribed. Every compile_fail doctest in sandbox.rs is paired with a passing example differing only in the property under test, and each was compiled standalone with rustc --edition 2024 against the crate rlib to confirm its error code: E0308 for the egress split, E0308 for a transposed digest domain, E0599 for the absent approval accessor, E0599 for the absent PathGrants::union, E0599 for the absent fourth quarantined operation, E0599 for the absent AdoptedHost constructor, E0063 for an omitted spec field and E0616 for assigning to a private spec field. Fourteen negative controls were run: each broke one behaviour, the matching test was observed to fail, and the source was restored and the test observed to pass again.
